rows.disposition: Historical2025heading replaced by explicit2026rates.

rows.old_text:
- **Employee social-insurance contributions** — 9.4% of gross remuneration (pension, sickness, disability, unemployment) percent  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Employee health-insurance contribution** — 4% of remuneration in 2025 (no maximum assessment base); reduced rates apply for persons with disabilities percent (Rises to 5% from 2026 — 2025 rate is 4%; confirm)  _(Act on Health Insurance (Act No. 580/2004 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Employer social-insurance contributions** — 24.4% of gross remuneration (excluding accident insurance) percent  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Employer accident insurance** — 0.8% of total payroll, with no maximum assessment base percent  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Employer health-insurance contribution** — 11% of remuneration, with no maximum assessment base percent  _(Act on Health Insurance (Act No. 580/2004 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Maximum monthly assessment base (social insurance)** — EUR 15,730 per month for 2025 (11x the average wage of two years prior) EUR (Applies to social insurance only; health insurance is uncapped)  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Maximum monthly employee social contribution** — Approx. EUR 1,478.62 per month (9.4% of the EUR 15,730 cap) EUR ((approx — derived from 2025 cap; confirm))  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Income tax withholding on wages (PAYE-equivalent)** — Employer withholds monthly advance income tax at 19% (and 25% above the monthly equivalent of the band), reconciled in the annual return or employer annual reconciliation  _(Income Tax Act (Act No. 595/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/taxes-on-personal-income)_
- **Contribution remittance deadline** — Social and health contributions are due on the employer's regular payday for the relevant month  _(Social Insurance Act (Act No. 461/2003 Coll.); Act on Health Insurance (Act No. 580/2004 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/other-taxes)_
- **Withheld wage tax remittance deadline** — By the 5th day after the wages are paid ((confirm exact statutory day))  _(Income Tax Act (Act No. 595/2003 Coll.) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/slovak-republic/individual/tax-administration)_

rows.old_text: Slovak payroll funds two systems: social insurance (Sociálna poisťovňa) and public health insurance. Employers withhold income tax and the employee's contributions monthly and remit them with their own employer contributions. Most social-insurance contributions are capped at a maximum monthly assessment base; health insurance is uncapped.

rows.old_text: Tax year: the calendar year. Currency: euro. Three bodies collect from a payroll: Sociálna poisťovňa (social insurance), the employee's own health insurer (VšZP, Dôvera or Union, supervised by ÚDZS) and the tax office (Finančná správa) for the wage tax advance. Each has its own registration, report and due date.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Employers.** Any person or company that pays an employee is a social insurance payer and deducts the employee's share (Act 461/2003 §§ 128, 141(2)). It is also a health insurance payer and computes and pays health advances for each employee (Act 580/2004 §16(2)(a), (c), (4)). An employer resident in Slovakia, or a foreign one with a Slovak branch, is the tax payer (platiteľ dane) and withholds the monthly tax advance (Act 595/2003 §35(1)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Employees.** People in an employment relationship (pracovný pomer) and people on work agreements (dohody). There is no minimum assessment base for an employee's social insurance: the base is the pay actually accounted (Act 461/2003 §138(1); Sociálna poisťovňa, 2026 tables, note 1). The employer must still pay at least the minimum wage under labour law: EUR 915 a month from 1 January 2026 ([Ministry of Labour, minimum wage 2026](https://www.employment.gov.sk/sk/uvodna-stranka/informacie-media/aktuality/historicky-narast-minimalnej-mzdy-je-realitou-roku-2026-je-minimalna-mzda-vo-vyske-915-eur.html)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
**Self-employed (SZČO).** From 1 January 2026 a person aged 18 or over is an SZČO for social insurance if they hold a licence to do business or, by an honest declaration, carry on self-employed work that needs no licence (for example an artist or author). Income no longer decides this status (Sociálna poisťovňa, changes from 1 January 2026, item 22).
- **New entrants** (no licence in the last 60 months) become compulsorily insured from the first day of the sixth calendar month after the month the licence starts.
- **Returning entrants** (a licence ended less than 60 months ago) are insured from the day the licence starts.
- Insurance now lasts until the licence ends. The old income test at 1 July no longer ends it.
- **Transition:** to 30 June 2026 an SZČO who held a licence before 1 January 2026 stays under the old rules. Under those rules insurance started on 1 July 2025 (1 October 2025 with an extended tax deadline) if 2024 income was above EUR 8,580 (Sociálna poisťovňa, 2026 tables, note 3).
rows.disposition: SZCO definition and start/end/Julytransition method retained with ownAct122/current21; former Januaryoverview coverage superseded precisely.

rows.old_text: Every SZČO pays health insurance advances from the start of the business (Act 580/2004 §16(2)(b), (8)(a)).
rows.disposition: Health advances frombusinessstart retained; no socialcoverage inference.

rows.old_text: **Not covered here.** Voluntary insurance (dobrovoľne poistená osoba), the special scheme for municipal police, and health insurance on dividends. See `slovakia-pit` for an SZČO's annual return.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Rounding.** Social insurance: each assessment base and each separate contribution is rounded down to the cent (Act 461/2003 §138(14); 2026 tables, closing note). Health: bases and advances are rounded down to the cent (Act 580/2004 §13(17), §16(1)). Income tax: amounts are rounded half up to two decimals (Act 595/2003 §47).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ## The taxable base
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Employee social base.** Pay from the work, except income that is not taxable or is exempt from income tax, and except employer contributions to supplementary pension saving (Act 461/2003 §138(1)). A profit share paid to an employee who holds no capital is included. The base is capped at EUR 16,764 a month; employer accident insurance runs on the full pay (§138(10)). From 2026 the employee and employer pay social insurance on any pay accounted during sickness, maternity or care leave. The old exclusion periods are gone for employees (Sociálna poisťovňa, changes from 1 January 2026, item 26). Where someone has several jobs, social contributions run from the highest base down (§138(12)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Employee health base.** The same employment income, with no ceiling (Act 580/2004 §13(1); VšZP, employer page). The employer's 11% runs on the gross before any deductible amount (§13(4), §16(2)(c)). The total employee and employer health advance must be at least EUR 45.45 for a full month; any shortfall is added to the employee's share (§16a).
rows.disposition: Employee health base/noceiling/allowance/minimumadvance preserved with actual excludedday gates.

rows.old_text: **Wage tax advance.** Taxable wage = gross taxable pay less the employee's social and health contributions, less EUR 497.23 if the employee has signed the declaration (vyhlásenie) with this employer (Act 595/2003 §35(1), (4), §36(6)). Only one employer may hold that declaration. The spouse allowance and pension savings deductions wait for the annual reconciliation (§35(1)(b)). Apply the monthly bands to the taxable wage, then reduce the advance by the child tax bonus (§35(2), (5)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Child tax bonus in payroll.** Granted only by the employer holding the declaration. It is capped at the §33(6) share of the month's employment tax base (gross less employee contributions), and the §33(11) taper applies to that monthly base (§35(5)). If the bonus exceeds the advance, the employer pays the difference from the tax it withheld for all staff. If that is not enough, it pays from its own money and claims the balance from the tax office after the quarter (§35(7)).
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **Net pay** = gross − employee social − employee health − tax advance after bonus. **Employer cost** = gross + employer social (with accident) + employer health.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
**SZČO social base** (Act 461/2003 §138(2)):
1. If last year's income from business (not profit) was above EUR 9,144: take the business tax base from the tax return, before deducting the social and health contributions paid. Divide it by 12, then by 1.486, and round down to the cent. The result is at least EUR 914.40 and at most EUR 16,764. It applies from 1 July of the year after the income year to 30 June of the next year, or from 1 October to 30 September with an extended tax deadline.
2. Otherwise, and for a new entrant, the special base of EUR 396.24 applies.
rows.disposition: Income-derived SZCO base and currentJuly coverage thresholds retained; exact2876.90end vs2876.91–9144specialbase.

rows.old_text: Each component (4.4%, 18%, 6%, 4.75%) is rounded down separately.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: **SZČO health advance.** 16% of the business tax base from two years earlier (2024 for 2026), taken before contributions paid, divided by the months of business in that year and by 1.486. The advance is at least EUR 121.92 (Act 580/2004 §16(2)(b), (3), (8)(a)). The insurer states the amount in the annual reconciliation. An SZČO who is also an employee pays their own SZČO advance, with no minimum (§16(6), (8)(e)).
rows.disposition: Rechecked current destination; prior 423-unit review disposition: F07 concurrentstateinsurance/below3advance

rows.old_text: ## Cross-border points
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
- **EU coordination.** Within the EU, EEA and Switzerland a person is subject to one country's social security law at a time (Regulation 883/2004 Art. 11(1)). A worker posted from Slovakia for work expected to last up to 24 months stays under Slovak law (Art. 12(1)) and carries an A1 form issued by Sociálna poisťovňa. A worker posted to Slovakia with a foreign A1 pays no Slovak social insurance.
- **Foreign employer.** A foreign employer with no Slovak branch is not the tax payer. A resident employee pays the tax advances themselves by the end of the next month (Act 595/2003 §35(10)). A non-resident does the same under §35(11), from the start of the stay if the contract shows more than 183 days.
- **Pay taxed abroad.** The employer withholds no advance on pay that is taxed abroad (Act 595/2003 §35(8)). The tax bonus needs at least 90% of total income from Slovak sources (§33(9)). Treaty conditions and documents are in `sk-cross-border`.

rows.old_text: ## Worked examples
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ### Example 1: employee, EUR 2,500 a month, one child aged 10
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Jana works full time under an employment contract. Her gross pay is EUR 2,500 a month. She signed the declaration with this employer, has one child aged 10, no disability, and earns nothing else.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Her pay is below EUR 16,764, so the social base is EUR 2,500. Employee social is 9.4% = EUR 235.00. Employee health is 5% = EUR 125.00. The taxable wage is 2,500 − 360 − 497.23 = EUR 1,642.77. That is below EUR 3,665.28, so the advance is 19% = EUR 312.13. The child bonus of EUR 100 is below the cap of 29% of EUR 2,140 (EUR 620.60). Her monthly base is below the EUR 2,286 taper point (EUR 27,432 / 12), so the bonus is not reduced. The advance falls to EUR 212.13. Net pay is EUR 1,927.87.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The employer pays 24.4% social (EUR 610.00), 0.8% accident (EUR 20.00) and 11% health (EUR 275.00). Employer cost is EUR 3,405.00. Sociálna poisťovňa receives EUR 865.00 on payday, the health insurer EUR 400.00, and the tax office EUR 212.13 within 5 days.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: ### Example 2: self-employed (SZČO) contributions from July 2026
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: Peter has been self-employed for years. His 2025 return shows business income of EUR 48,000 and a tax base of EUR 21,000, after deducting EUR 7,500 of social and health contributions he paid in 2025. His 2024 return showed a tax base of EUR 24,000 before contributions, for 12 months of business. He has no extended filing deadline and no disability.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: His 2025 income is above EUR 9,144, so the 1.486 method applies. The tax base before contributions is 21,000 + 7,500 = EUR 28,500. That gives 28,500 / 12 = EUR 2,375, and 2,375 / 1.486 = EUR 1,598.25 (rounded down). This is between EUR 914.40 and EUR 16,764. From July 2026 to June 2027 he pays EUR 70.32 sickness, EUR 287.68 old age, EUR 95.89 disability and EUR 75.91 reserve fund: EUR 529.80 a month, each due by the 8th of the next month.
rows.disposition: Rechecked current destination; prior 423-unit review disposition: F17 contributioncalendarboundarieswithoutchangingincome-derivedfigure

rows.old_text: His 2026 health advance uses 2024: 24,000 / 12 / 1.486 = EUR 1,345.89, and 16% gives EUR 215.34 a month. That is above the EUR 121.92 minimum.
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text: The edge case: if his 2025 income had been EUR 9,144 or less, he would pay on the EUR 396.24 special base, EUR 131.34 a month, not on the EUR 914.40 minimum.

rows.old_text: ## Ask the client first
rows.disposition: Exact retained unit; all embedded topics preserved.

rows.old_text:
1. **Contract type for each worker.** Employment contract, work agreement (dohoda) or self-employed. This changes the unemployment and support rates, the EUR 200 deduction and the health deductible amount.
2. **Has the employee signed the tax declaration with you, and which children (with ages) are claimed?** Only one employer gives the EUR 497.23 allowance and the tax bonus.
3. **Disability, pension or second-pillar status.** Disability halves the health rates; a pensioner pays no disability or unemployment insurance; a saver's 4% goes to the pension fund.
4. **Your payday.** Social and health payments fall due on it; the tax advance 5 days later.
5. **For an SZČO: the date the licence started, any licence that ended in the last 60 months, the last two returns (income, tax base, contributions deducted) and any extended filing deadline.** These set the start date and both bases.
6. **Any work abroad, A1 form or foreign employer.** This changes who collects.
